name: codezen
summary: CodeZen is an AI-powered code plugin to build software with skills.
problem: Agent-assisted work tends to jump straight to code. Requirements stay half-specified, and tests and deployment become an afterthought.
benefits: Covers requirements, build, test and deploy, so the work either side of writing code is part of the process.
Korza's own plugin, so the conventions it applies are the ones your reviewers already expect.
Depends on superpowers and pyright-lsp, so installing codezen brings both along.

name: pyright-lsp
summary: Pyright LSP plugin used in codezen.
problem: Without a language server the agent reads Python as plain text. It infers signatures instead of looking them up, and type errors an IDE would flag immediately go unnoticed.
benefits: Gives the agent real diagnostics and type information on Python code.
Maintained in Anthropic's official plugin repo rather than by us.
codezen already depends on it, so install this directly only if you skip codezen.

name: superpowers
summary: Core skills library: TDD, debugging, collaboration patterns. Referred by codezen.
problem: Left to itself, an agent writes code first and reasons about it afterwards. The result reads well and fails under test.
benefits: A vetted library of TDD, debugging and collaboration patterns, so the approach is not improvised on every task.
Pinned to v6.2.0, so upstream commits cannot land on your machine unreviewed.
codezen builds on it, so the two are designed to run together.

name: mattpocock-skills
summary: Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity skills: TDD, code review, domain modeling, bug diagnosis, grilling and more.
problem: The jobs around writing code get re-improvised every time: reviewing a PR, diagnosing a bug, turning a spec into tickets, handing work over. How well they go depends on who asked and how.
benefits: Twenty-five task-specific skills covering review, TDD, domain modelling, triage and architecture.
Includes the communication side of the work: teaching, handoffs, questionnaires, writing for agents.
Tracks main on purpose, because the newest tag ships four fewer skills.

name: humanizer
summary: Removes signs of AI-generated writing from text, based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" guide.
problem: AI prose has tells: inflated symbolism, promotional language, em dash overuse, the rule of three, filler phrases. Readers notice them even when they cannot name them.
benefits: Edits against Wikipedia's documented "Signs of AI writing" list rather than a vague sense of tone.
Worth running on anything customer-facing: docs, release notes, incident writeups.
